11.1.b:
MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "how do you know a total knee is balanced?"
- "Trials in → **full motion**, **rectangular** equal gaps, stable to stress, patella tracking."
- "**Coronal** = medial vs lateral · **sagittal** = flexion vs extension gap → answer both."
- "Osteophytes off, bone cut, then release the **concave, tight side** stepwise · cuts → chapter 10."

### What a balanced knee shows
| Criterion | Requirement |
|---|---|
| **Motion** | full range → 0–110/120° PS (posterior-stabilised), slightly less CR (cruciate-retaining) |
| **Gap shape** | **rectangular** → flexion = extension · medial = lateral |
| **Coronal stability** | negative varus–valgus stress test |
| **Patella** | normal tracking → tilt or towel-clip test |

- Judge with **trials** and spacers, not cuts alone → the construct shows real soft-tissue behaviour
- Trial reduction → trials + thin insert → releases → recheck at **90° and 45°** (Prof Sherief Khaled)
[[FIG: Fig 11.1 · 11.1
- Goal → **1–2 mm** balanced varus–valgus opening each side · recheck after each release (Campbell)
- After cement sets → trial insert again → stability, motion, patellar tracking, collaterals in flexion

#### Mid-flexion — the angle most often missed
- **Mid-flexion instability** → stable at 0° and 90°, lax near 45° → insert lifts forward
- Cause → tight posterior capsule + extra distal cut → **joint line raised** >4 mm (Campbell)
- Show of hands → only two attendees test mid-flexion (Prof Sherief Khaled)
- Case → trial unstable at 45° → insert **12 → 17 mm** + **MCL** (medial collateral ligament) plication
[[FIG: Fig 11.2 · 11.1

#### Gap tools
- **Spacer blocks** are company-specific → J&J blue block for extension, motion block 1 mm smaller for flexion
[[FIG: Fig 11.3 · 11.1
- Blue block for both gaps = error → know your system
- **Laminar spreaders** → gap shape before femoral rotation · two, opposed · osteoporotic bone → at the **rim**
- **Finger test** → traction, index finger in each space · flexion gap at 90°, after chamfers

#### What the insert size tells you
- Extension block **10** enters → usually a 12 insert · **9** → usually 10 (Prof Shokry)
[[FIG: Fig 11.4 · 11.1
- Insert **10–12** ideal → joint line restored · 9 → borderline: cut or release problem
- Insert **14** → laxity · **17+** → one gap larger, poor cuts compensated by the insert

### Why balance matters
- TKA (total knee arthroplasty) = "**a surgery of soft-tissue balancing**" → its most important step (Prof Sherief Khaled)
[[FIG: Fig 11.5 · 11.1
- Balanced → load shared by both condyles → durability · unbalanced → one-sided load, wear
- Any technique without balancing → early failure, ≈**3 months** (Prof Abd Elkarim)
- Tight collateral or PCL (posterior cruciate ligament) → stiffness · lax → **instability** → early revision

#### Instability picture
- **Giving way**, recurrent effusion, diffuse peri-retinacular tenderness

### Coronal balance — rectangle, not trapezoid
- **Rectangular** gaps in extension and flexion → equal medial and lateral load
[[FIG: Fig 11.6 · 11.1
- **Trapezoidal** gap → tight side overloaded → polyethylene wear → early failure
- **Condylar lift-off** under stress → eccentric load → test at 0°, 30°, 60°, 90° (Prof Sherief Khaled)
- Flexion-gap shape also follows **femoral rotation** → internal rotation: medial tight, lateral loose
[[FIG: Fig 11.7 · 11.1

#### Varus or valgus
- **Varus** → medial tight, lateral open · **valgus** → lateral tight, medial open
- Rule → release the **concave, tight** side · fill the convex, stretched side with implant
- Stress films → asymmetric opening · correctable deformity → less release than a fixed one
- Long-standing valgus → **attenuated MCL** → incompetent after lateral release → more constraint (Campbell)

#### Both sides tight = bone problem
- Not even block 9 enters → **cut error** → re-cut, never bilateral releases (Prof Shokry)
- Finger test → both sides tight: bony cut · medial only: soft tissue

### Before any release
- Remove all **osteophytes** first → they tent capsule and collaterals → removal alone may balance (Campbell)
[[FIG: Fig 11.8 · 11.1
- Releasing before osteophyte removal → false tightness → over-release
- **Posterior osteophytes** → flexion stops ≈90°, capsule tented → contracture · lateral film shows them
- Posterior femoral ones → removed through the flexion gap after the femoral cuts

#### Timing
- No early release, no skeletonised tibia → cut first, then judge (Prof Sherief Khaled)
- **Medial tibial overhang** → tents the MCL, spoils the release → irritation, arthrofibrosis
- Release **stepwise**, recheck each step → over-release cannot be undone without constraint

PITFALL — trapezoid flexion gap: ligament or rotation?
- Internally rotated femur → medial flexion gap tight, lateral loose → mimics medial contracture
- Say → "**check femoral rotation first, then release the medial side in flexion**"

HIGH YIELD — Memory line
- **Rectangle · 1–2 mm · test 45° · osteophytes first · concave side · both tight = bone**

11.2.b:
MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "how do you release a varus and a valgus knee?"
- "Varus → **medial**, off the tibia: deep MCL → posteromedial corner → superficial MCL → pes."
- "Valgus → **lateral**, off the femur: posterolateral capsule → **ITB** → **popliteus** → LCL last."
- "Posterior structures open **extension**, anterior ones **flexion** · over-release → constraint."

### Varus — medial release
- Find the tight gap → **posteromedial corner** tight in extension · **anterior superficial MCL** in flexion (Miller)
[[FIG: Fig 11.9 · 11.2
- **Semimembranosus** → several posteromedial insertions · with POL (posterior oblique ligament) = posteromedial corner

| Medial tightness (Handbook) | Release |
|---|---|
| <2 mm | medial capsule + **deep MCL** |
| 2–4 mm | extension → posteromedial corner · flexion → anterior superficial MCL |
| 4–6 mm | whole **superficial MCL** |
| 6–8 mm | all the above |
| >8 mm | + **pes anserinus** (sartorius, gracilis, semitendinosus) |

#### Stepwise at the table
- Block enters laterally only → **medial contracture** → release, re-examine until medial = lateral
- Osteophytes → upper MCL + pes, subperiosteal → posterior deep MCL → posteromedial capsule (Prof Shokry)
- Still tense → capsular corner peeled off bone → tibia externally rotates
- Prof Sherief Khaled → osteophytes → periosteal sleeve → posteromedial capsule + POL → semimembranosus

#### By structure and by design
- Anterior superficial MCL + pes → **flexion** gap · posterior half, POL, semimembranosus → **extension**
- **PS** → PCL resected first, a secondary medial stabiliser → less release, never the whole sleeve
[[FIG: Fig 11.10 · 11.2
- **CR**, tight flexion → anterior superficial MCL + pes → PCL → posterior capsule
- Whole sleeve released, still tight → advance the **LCL** (lateral collateral ligament) or add constraint

#### Technique & limits
- Off the **tibia**, elevator or osteotome → the long MCL footprint lifts stepwise
- Periosteum lifted **2–3 cm** → deep MCL free, superficial MCL intact (Prof Sherief Khaled)
- Superficial MCL lifted top-down, ≤**8 cm** → never detached completely (Prof Shokry)
- **Medial reduction osteotomy** → medial plateau rim off, tray downsized or lateralised → MCL spared

PITFALL — the over-released medial sleeve
- Superficial MCL over-released → **flexion instability** → standard insert no longer holds
- Say → "**stepwise, recheck every step · incompetent MCL → constrained condylar implant**"

### Pie-crusting
- Multiple **stab incisions**, blade or needle, parallel to the joint line → lengthen taut fibres
[[FIG: Fig 11.11 · 11.2
- Lateral pie-crusting leaves a **tether** → no big lateral flexion opening until LCL cut
- Varus → pie-crusting not enough → classic subperiosteal tibial release
- **Peroneal nerve** within **1.5 cm** of posterolateral corner → pie-crust knee **flexed** (Campbell)

### Valgus — lateral release
- Assess after osteophytes and meniscus out · **Ranawat** classification → deformity size and MCL competence
- Releases fix soft tissue only → **bony deformity** needs a cut or osteotomy
- Off the **femur**, sharp → LCL and popliteus share a small epicondylar origin
- **Popliteus** inserts anterior and distal to the LCL origin (Miller)
[[FIG: Fig 11.12 · 11.2

| Tight in | Release (Campbell, Miller) |
|---|---|
| **Extension** | **ITB** (iliotibial band) → pie-crust, not transect · posterolateral capsule · posterior capsule off femur |
| **Flexion** | **popliteus** |
| **Both** | **LCL** → last |
| Still tight in extension | lateral head of **gastrocnemius** |

#### Order — the surgeon's school
- PS → PCL out → pie-crust posterolateral capsule → ITB or popliteus first
- Sports surgeon → ITB first, popliteus last · arthroplasty surgeon → popliteus first, ITB last
- Campbell → spare a slack popliteus · small correction → posterolateral corner before LCL
- Extension only → pie-crust the ITB, check the **biceps** aponeurosis

#### When releases are not enough
- PCL often attenuated in valgus · still unbalanced → inspect it → **MCL advancement**
[[FIG: Fig 11.13 · 11.2
- Lateral flexion gap > extension → PS post **jump height** → constrained condylar (Campbell)
- Elderly, lax MCL → constrained condylar · no routine **CCK** → 15° ≠ 50° (Prof Sherief Khaled)
- Severe valgus + contracture → **peroneal nerve** stretch → palsy: flex knee, loosen dressings

HIGH YIELD — Memory line
- **Varus: tibia, deep MCL → POL → sMCL → pes · valgus: femur, ITB extension, popliteus flexion, LCL last**

11.3.b:
MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "how do you balance the flexion and extension gaps?"
- "**Tibia** → both gaps · **distal femur** → extension · posterior femur, size, slope, PCL → flexion."
- "**McPherson rule** → symmetric problem: fix the tibia · asymmetric problem: fix the femur."
- "Tight → cut or release · loose → add back: thicker insert, bigger femur, augment."

### Principles
- Tight extension → no straightening · tight flexion → no bending · loose → unstable
- Small difference fine · flexion slightly tighter matters little
- **Recurvatum** = loose extension gap · loose PS flexion gap → **cam jump**

### What moves each gap
| Gap | Controlled by (Miller) |
|---|---|
| **Both** | **tibial cut** · insert thickness |
| **Extension** only | **distal femoral cut** · posterior capsule, gastrocnemius |
| **Flexion** only | **posterior femoral cut** · femoral AP (anteroposterior) size · **PCL** in CR · tibial slope |

- Undersized femur → instability · oversized → lost flexion
[[FIG: Fig 11.14 · 11.3
- Downsizing with **posterior referencing** → anterior **notching** → use anterior referencing
- **Posterior capsule** stripped after the femoral cuts → curved instrument, guard the neurovascular bundle
[[FIG: Fig 11.15 · 11.3

#### The PCL in the flexion gap
- PCL release → flexion gap +**4–6 mm**, extension <2 mm (Campbell)
- Tight PCL → trial tray **lifts off** in flexion · at 90° it deflects **1–2 mm** to pressure
[[FIG: Fig 11.16 · 11.3
- **Recession** → stepwise, subperiosteal, 1–2 mm steps off the tibial bone island
- Retained PCL, tight flexion → snips, recheck rollback · PS → clear the PCL remnants

#### When the PCL is the wrong lever
- Partial release fails → check slope, or smaller femur with anterior referencing
- Incompetent PCL → **PS** or deep-dish · >**75%** released → more posterior constraint
- Slope outweighs partial PCL release · PCL release never corrects a **flexion contracture**

### McPherson rule
- **Symmetric** gap problem → adjust the **tibia** · **asymmetric** → adjust the **femur** (Miller)
- Wrong bone → two problems → tight extension fixed by tibia → flexion loose too
- Smallest block won't enter, flexion fine → re-cut the **femur**
- Equal gaps, too tight → more proximal tibia · equal but lax → thicker insert

### Single-gap patterns
| Pattern | Management |
|---|---|
| Tight both | cut more **tibia** |
| Loose both | thicker **insert** · tibial augments |
| Tight extension, flexion good | osteophytes + **posterior capsule** → then distal femur +2 mm |
| Loose extension, flexion good | **distal femoral augment** |
| Tight flexion, extension good | PCL/capsule → ↑ slope → downsize femur or more posterior cut |
| Loose flexion, extension good | **upsize femur** · posterior augment |

- Two questions → which gap, tight or loose · drawn for every scenario
[[FIG: Fig 11.17 · 11.3

#### Tight extension — how much bone
- Distal femur +**2 mm** only, then tibia → repeated femoral recuts raise the joint line (Prof Sherief Khaled)
[[FIG: Fig 11.18 · 11.3
- Allowance → femur +2, tibia +2–4 mm · very tight: tibia +5–6, femur +4 mm
- Hardest → short, small-built men with a **flexion deformity**
- **FFD** (fixed flexion deformity) → extra distal femur **2 mm** at a time · recurvatum → less, 7 vs 8–10 mm
[[FIG: Fig 11.19 · 11.3

PITFALL — how much distal femur for a contracture?
- Course → +2 mm, 4 if very tight · Campbell → max **4 mm** · Miller → 2 mm ≈ **10°**
- Say → "**capsule first, then distal femur 2 mm at a time, never past 4 mm**"

#### Tight flexion — order of steps
- Soft tissue → tibial **slope** → posterior condyles last → offset kept (Prof Sherief Khaled)
- **4-in-1 block** on the +2 hole → 2 mm more posterior condyle
[[FIG: Fig 11.20 · 11.3
- Downsizing → AP only · posterior condyles cut for the next size, **anterior referencing** (Campbell)

#### Loose gaps — add back
- Loose flexion → **upsize femur** · same size + thicker insert → spoils extension
- **Posterior augments** → same effect · often only on a **stemmed** femur
- Loose extension → distal augment → lowers a raised joint line

### Mixed patterns — two strategies
| Pattern | Strategy 1 → fix each gap at source | Strategy 2 → loosen, then fill |
|---|---|---|
| Loose flexion + tight extension | distal cut or capsule + **upsize femur** | loosen extension → thicker insert |
| Tight flexion + loose extension | posterior cut or downsize + **distal augment** | loosen flexion → thicker insert |

- Strategy 1 keeps the **joint line** · Strategy 2 simpler, may move it
- Upsizing → mediolateral overhang, **patellofemoral overstuffing**
- Thick insert in an enlarged extension gap → joint line up → **pseudo-patella baja**

#### Recurvatum
- No neuromuscular weakness → joint line **3–5 mm** distal + smaller femur, anterior referencing (Campbell)
- Ten patients corrected this way → none recurred at 1 year
- Technique → 2–3 mm less distal femur · between sizes → smaller femur
- Neuromuscular or quadriceps weakness → recurs → **hinge** with an extension stop

HIGH YIELD — Memory line
- **Tibia both · distal femur extension · rest flexion · symmetric tibia, asymmetric femur**

- Upsizing → mediolateral overhang, **patellofemoral overstuffing**
- Thick insert in an enlarged extension gap → joint line up → **pseudo-patella baja**

#### Recurvatum
- No neuromuscular weakness → joint line **3–5 mm** distal + smaller femur, anterior referencing (Campbell)
- Ten patients corrected this way → none recurred at 1 year
- Technique → 2–3 mm less distal femur · between sizes → smaller femur
- Neuromuscular or quadriceps weakness → recurs → **hinge** with an extension stop

HIGH YIELD — Memory line
- **Tibia both · distal femur extension · rest flexion · symmetric tibia, asymmetric femur**
